We need to find a retrosynthetic template that when applied to target molecule (given SMILES) reproduces the Peterson reaction reverse: target is alkene with phenyl groups and methoxy? SMILES: C=C(C1=CC=C(OC)C=C1)C2=CC=C(OC)C=C2. That's a stilbene derivative with two anisole rings (para-methoxy phenyl). The forward Peterson: from beta-hydroxy silane to alkene, losing SiMe3 and OH (as water). So retrosynthesis: break C=C double bond to give a beta-hydroxy silane precursor: an alkene carbon attached to SiMe3 and OH on adjacent carbon? Actually Peterson: alpha-silyl carbanion adds to carbonyl to give beta-hydroxy silane, then elimination gives alkene, losing SiMe3OH? The transformation: C=C formed, breaking C-Si and C-O bonds. So template: break C=C into C-Si and C-O. Need template ID. Use search_template_catalog_by_criteria with functional_groups_broken = ["alkene"]? Wait forward reaction forms alkene, breaks carbon-silicon and carbon-oxygen. So broken groups: "silane", "alcohol"? Formed: "alkene". Also bonds broken: C-Si, C-O. Bonds formed: C=C. So criteria: functional_groups_broken maybe ["silane","alcohol"]; functional_groups_formed ["alkene"]; bonds_broken maybe ["6-6","6-8"]? Not sure.

Let's try search with functional_groups_broken=["silane","alcohol"], functional_groups_formed=["alkene"].
